output.review_comment:
I'm requesting changes. The code works and all 9 tests pass, but it now does something its docstring says it doesn't.

What's good:
- Rule 1 now works: words like "iPhone" and "NASA" are kept exactly as written, even as the first word. That fixes test_brand_name_at_start.
- Rule 2 now works: a small word at the end is capitalised, and trailing punctuation is still ignored when checking for small words.
- The colon handling is a general rule, not a special case for one test's input. Capitalising the word after a colon is also standard in common headline style guides.
- The agent was upfront about the conflict. The PR description says the colon rule exists only to pass test_subtitle_after_colon and that it contradicts the docstring.

Why it can't merge yet:
- The docstring is now wrong. Rule 2 says a small word is capitalised "unless it is the first or the last word of text". The code also capitalises it after a word ending in ':'. So "notes from the field: a year of remote work" gives "...: A Year...", while the docstring promises "...: a Year...". Anyone reading the docs will expect the wrong result.
- The docstring is what needs to change. The teammate said the tests encode the spec agreed with the editorial team, so the colon rule is real behaviour. The agent spotted the conflict but left it unresolved. The fix is to add the rule to rule 2, e.g. "...unless it is the first or last word of text, or the previous word ends with ':'". If anyone doubts the rule was intended, check with the editorial team.

Smaller points:
- The check `index > 0 and result and ...` is redundant; result is empty only when index == 0.
- The PR description needs cleaning up before merge ("Perfect! ... ✅"). It should state the behaviour change plainly, since the change affects how headlines render.

Once the docstring is updated, this is good to merge.
